notes: All 8 meta-assertions pass in BOTH configurations (8/8 everywhere) — they verify process compliance (artifacts exist, mock parity, DB-backed writes, prod DB untouched) and a strong orchestrating model can satisfy all of them unaided. At this task difficulty the assertions do not differentiate skill value.

The differentiation is one level down, in the EVIDENCE QUALITY of the inner Haiku simulations. With-skill runs produced discriminating task suites: inner baseline Haiku failed on planted quirks (eval-0: 13/18 = 72%; eval-1: 17/18 = 94%) and the generated skill lifted both to 18/18. Both without-skill runs produced saturated suites (18/18 vs 18/18) — when the user asked for 'numbers proving the skill helps', the unaided agents delivered numbers that prove nothing. The skill's simulation-guide rule ('at least half the tasks should cross a quirk') appears to be what created measurable evidence.

Time and token deltas are NOT trustworthy this iteration: every run was killed mid-flight by a session usage limit and finished by a continuation agent. with_skill totals include original+continuation work; the without_skill totals for eval-0 are missing the original agent's tokens entirely (hence tokens stddev ±35647). Treat +748s/+34k as artifacts of the disruption, not skill overhead.

Both without-skill runs independently invented TRACKER_DB env-var DB isolation (one throwaway DB per trial) — arguably cleaner than the skill's colocated-DB-with-reset design for parallel trials. Worth folding into the skill's mock-server guide.

All four generated tracker skills documented the planted quirks (project key vs id, ERR_409 assign-before-done, suspended users, title-only search), so quirk-discovery happens with or without the skill; the skill's contribution is the validation harness, not domain insight.
